## Course structure {.smaller .center}

**Lectures**

- Teacher presentations
- Literature
- Exercises in R

**Workshops**

- Teacher and student presentations
- Literature
- Assignments in R

**Group project**

- Data analysis with R
- Supervision

## Code of Conduct {.smaller}

- Everyone should feel respected
- All questions are appreciated and will be addressed (if time allow)
- Be helpful to each other - you learn more this way
- Teachers try using appropriate tone - please call us out if we're being
  boomers so we can be better!
- We dedicate a lot of time to this course but also teach other courses - please
  be patient with us if we do not answer email immediately

## How to study {.smaller}

**Lectures**

- Read literature **before**
- Read lecture notes **before or after**
- Teacher cover 50-75% of reading material (the most deficult part)
- **you self-study the rest**
- Exercises cover curriculum (aka exam-relevant)

**Exercises**

- Group work in class
- Teacher will help with everything we can (ask all you want)

## Getting or asking for help :raising_hand_woman::raising_hand_man: {.smaller}

::: {.r-stretch}
- There are lots of helpers
- Table mates, try to help out too
- We're all learning here!
  - This is a supportive and safe environment
  - Remember our Code of Conduct
- When you are IRL use humans
- When alone at home use chat models
:::

## Using chat models and AI {.smaller}

::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
**Do**

- Prompt to explain concept differently (the teacher said "X" - can you
  reformulate?)
- Prompt to explain code (here is some R code - ELI5 what does it do?)
- Prompt to probe your own knowledge (give me more assignments on "X")
- Use AI to challenge your understanding: "What assumptions am I making?"
- Ask for hints when you are stuck --- before asking for the solution.
:::::
::::: {.column width="50%"}
**Don't**

- Relying on help will make you dependent (what happens when AI is not there?)
- Trust any answer. A fluent and confident answer is not necessarily a correct
  answer. **you are responsible** for using any code or information.
- Please use each other and the teachers - otherwise, your education might be
  ONLY chat model AI in the future...
- Don't ask AI to simply solve every exercise. The solved exercise is not the
  goal. Learning is.
- Don't try to teach an LLM medical statistics. It already has plenty of
  opinions --- your job is to develop your own statistical reasoning.
:::::
:::

## More on chatmodels and AI {.smaller .scrollable}

See the website chapter
[5.2](https://danmazjen.github.io/medicinsk-statistik/pre-course/reading.html#using-ai)

**Further resources on responsible use of AI**

- [AAU: Generative AI for
  students](https://www.en.aub.aau.dk/students/generative-ai) --- guidance on
  academic practice, privacy, evaluating AI, useful scenarios, prompting, and
  avoiding over-reliance on AI.
- [AAU: Rules for use of generative
  AI](https://www.studerende.aau.dk/regler-og-praktisk/regler/regler-for-brug-af-generativ-ai) ---
  know the rules that apply to your studies and exams.
- [AAU: Scenarios for using generative
  AI](https://www.en.aub.aau.dk/students/generative-ai/scenarios-for-use) ---
  examples of appropriate uses of AI for studying, understanding difficult
  material, and exam preparation.
- [UNESCO: Guidance for generative AI in education and
  research](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/guidance-generative-ai-education-and-research) ---
  a broader perspective on human-centred and responsible use of generative AI in
  education.
